rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=6, train_n=200, n_iter=300, val_n=16, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.0001, unet_c=16, outer_wall_s=1500, seed=7, rationale=iter-12 NOISE-FLOOR CONFIRMATION (explicitly a confirmation, not a new lever): ONE knob seed 42->7 on the iter-4 ep6 PEAK cfg (ep6, lr=1e-4, c16, n_iter300, val_n16, grad_clip1.0, seed42 -> 0.9596). NO genuinely-untried LIVE per-image knob remains: every optimization/capacity/read axis has been swept in BOTH directions and all sit within noise of the ep6 peak -- lr anchored 1e-4 (iter-3 0.9553->0.9593; n_iter HURTS via per-scan overfit, no early-stop, iter-2 n_iter600 0.9553->0.9407); pretrain_epochs ep6 PEAK (ep3->6 up 0.9596, ep9 DOWN 0.9593 iter-10, ep12 down 0.9585 iter-5); unet_c flat (iter-6 c16->c32 0.9596->0.9495); grad_clip insensitive in BOTH directions (iter-8 tighter 0.5=0.9597, iter-11 looser 2.0=0.9592); val_n a read knob not a lever (iter-9 val_n24 0.9609); warm_start LOAD-BEARING-POSITIVE, kept True NEVER off. The config's `optimizer` field is a DEAD knob -- both the warm-start pre-pass and _fit_one_scene HARDCODE torch.optim.Adam and never read cfg['optimizer'], and there is no lr-scheduler hook in the solver; activating either would require editing the shared solver_dual_ddomain_n2i.py, which is FORBIDDEN. So per the iter-12 mandate fallback, this is a clean noise-floor confirmation: a THIRD independent seed at the peak config, turning the seed axis into a 3-point distribution (seed42=0.9596, seed123=0.9588 iter-7, seed7=?). Failure mode: per-image U-Net N2I on dense-view 128-angle breast is STRUCTURALLY FBP-BOUNDED -- the half-angle view-split discards information the full-view 128-view LD-FBP keeps, so each per-scan GT-free fit caps BELOW the LD-FBP baseline (hr=0); a substrate ceiling, not an optimization/capacity one. Hypothesis: seed=7 lands WITHIN NOISE of the ep6 peak (~0.958-0.960, hr=0), giving a 3-draw seed band whose width quantifies the ~0.96 breast per-image U-Net N2I noise floor and confirms the ceiling is real + seed-stable, not a single-draw artefact -- toward the iter-20 ceiling-documentation mandate. A material drop/lift would mean the per-scan fit is seed-fragile (a stability note, still not a climbable lever). Wall: iter-7 (seed123, same cfg) ran ~470s; identical except the seed value -> est ~470-500s, well under the 900s/15-min wall (outer_wall_s=1500 hard cap).
